question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Numerous writings by the ancient Greek astronomer Hipparchus (2nd century BCE) are ______ his Commentary, which critiques a well-known astronomical poem, is a surviving work: it can still be read today.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period ends the first independent clause and 'Conversely' introduces the contrasting second sentence.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? German sculptor Cornelia Konrads makes artworks that appear to belong to their surroundings. Her piece titled red pavilion is installed at a birdwatching pavilion in Taiwan. ______ resembling a set of red bamboo columns that seem to support the pavilion, the work is cleverly worked into its environment and serves as an example of Konrads's approach.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'For instance' presents the sculpture as an example of Konrads's approach.

question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim? A group of public transit specialists in Detroit is designing a new streetcar stop for the Woodward Avenue Streetcar system to serve a neighborhood that currently lacks one. To determine the stop's location, the group is relying on a decade-old survey that asked local residents how far they would be willing to walk to reach a streetcar stop. The group also reviewed research indicating that a person's willingness to walk to public transit depends on factors such as weather and whether paved sidewalks and crosswalks are available. One researcher contends that the survey no longer captures how the neighborhood's present-day residents feel.
option a: Over the past decade, the quantity of sidewalks and crosswalks in the neighborhood the new stop will serve has grown considerably.
option b: People in Detroit are far less inclined to ride public transit when it rains than when the weather is clear.
option c: During the last ten years, the number of cyclists using the roads in the neighborhood the new stop will serve has risen sharply.
option d: People who currently ride the Woodward Avenue Streetcar are content with how many stops the line has.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: More sidewalks and crosswalks since the survey would change residents' willingness to walk, making the old survey inaccurate.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
Brown Bears in Katmai National Park, Alaska
Bear identification number | Sex | Age (years) | Approximate weight (pounds)
120 | female | 8 | 400
184 | male | 9 | 800
115 | female | 4 | 325
104 | female | 14 | 425
Researchers gathered data on brown bears living in Katmai National Park, Alaska, recording each bear's sex, age, and approximate weight. According to the table, the bear listed with the highest approximate weight was the one with identification number ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Bear 184's approximate weight of 800 pounds is the highest in the table.

question: Which quotation from Life Among the Paiutes most effectively illustrates the claim? Life Among the Paiutes is an 1882 autobiographical account by Sarah Winnemucca Hopkins, a Northern Paiute writer, teacher, and activist. Throughout the book, Winnemucca speaks straight to her audience in order to describe particular customs, as when she writes ______
option a: "But how can I describe the scene that followed? Some of you, dear readers, can imagine."
option b: "We would all go in company to see if the flowers we were named for were yet in bloom, for almost all the girls are named for flowers."
option c: "During the time my grandfather was away in California, where he [stayed] till after the Mexican war, there was a girl-baby born in our family."
option d: "Now, my dear reader, there is no word so endearing as the word father, and that is why [my people] call all good people father or mother."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: This quotation directly addresses the reader while explaining a Paiute custom.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "breathes" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from the 1895 poem "Ojistoh" by Emily Pauline Johnson, a Kanienkahagen (Mohawk) writer who also went by the name Tekahionwake.
I am Ojistoh, I am she, the wife Of him whose name breathes bravery and life And courage to the tribe who calls him chief. I am Ojistoh, his white star, and he Is land, and lake, and sky--and soul to me.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Breathes ... bravery and life' means the name imparts those qualities to the tribe.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? As volcanologists such as Tamsin Mather often point out, volcanoes are not all alike. Lanzarote in Spain, for instance, is a fissure vent--a linear opening from which lava flows, typically without explosive activity. Qualibou in Saint Lucia, ______ is a caldera--a large, cauldron-shaped depression that forms soon after a magma chamber empties during a volcanic eruption.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'In contrast' marks the difference between a fissure vent and a caldera.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In an investigation into how music tempo (measured in beats per minute, or bpm) affects exercise, participants cycled for 30 minutes while continuously listening to Beyoncé's "Irreplaceable" (88 bpm). The researchers expected that the next day, when participants did the same workout while listening to Led Zeppelin's "Rock and Roll" (169 bpm), they would pedal faster. However, the participants' second-day performance may have been hindered by fatigue carried over from the first day. Therefore, ______
option a: how well participants already knew the songs may have played a role in the performance differences between the two days.
option b: the researchers could not precisely gauge how fast participants pedaled on the second day.
option c: participants showed that they favored one of the songs more than the other.
option d: the second day's findings might cause the impact of the faster song to be underestimated.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Day-two fatigue would suppress speed, so the faster song's real effect is underestimated.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In Burkina Faso, a country in West Africa, the share of the population residing in cities grew from 27.5% to 30.6% between 2015 and 2020. ______ urbanization rates increased throughout West Africa as a whole, climbing 3.2 percentage points over those five years.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Concurrently' shows the region-wide urbanization rose during the same period.

question: According to the text, where do Huang and colleagues think K. popovi adults kept their eggs? Although seed shrimp and certain other arthropods have long been recognized for actively tending their eggs and young, comparatively little has been understood about such behavior in ancient insects. Diying Huang and colleagues now argue that Jurassic fossils from a Chinese site preserve the oldest known evidence of insect brood care. Studying fossils of Karataviella popovi, an extinct aquatic insect, the researchers identified thirty adults that appear to have carried clusters of eggs on one of their left legs. The find indicates that insects practiced brood care far earlier than had been thought.
option a: On plants beneath the water's surface
option b: On a pair of their right legs
option c: On one of their left legs
option d: On the fossilized remains of other insects
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage states the adults kept egg clusters on one of their left legs.

question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two games. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has compiled these notes: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island is a board game drawn from the writing of Daniel Defoe; it includes characters and events from Defoe's novel Robinson Crusoe. Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell is a board game drawn from the writing of Susanna Clarke; it includes characters and events from Clarke's novel Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell.
option a: The board game Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island, which draws on Daniel Defoe's writing, includes characters and events from the novel Robinson Crusoe.
option b: Certain board games incorporate characters and events from fictional works; Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, for instance, is based on Susanna Clarke's novel Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell.
option c: The game Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island and the game Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell both feature themes drawn from works of fiction.
option d: Whereas the game Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island draws on a work by Daniel Defoe, the game Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell draws on a work by Susanna Clarke.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice D highlights that the two games are based on works by different authors.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? A river's hyporheic zone (HZ)--a distinctive habitat where surface water and groundwater meet within river corridors--reaches beyond the river's banks; for a major river such as the Brahmaputra, the HZ may extend as far as 400 meters from the channel. Because the zone is so difficult to access, scientists rely on ______ to gauge it--for instance, by mapping the aquatic organisms found in soil well beyond a waterway's banks.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Proxies' fits the indirect measurement (mapping organisms) used for the inaccessible zone.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? Earlier studies of writing samples from participants had revealed a connection between aging and, among other linguistic changes, greater use of present-tense verbs (e.g., "goes"). Building on this, two researchers set out to determine whether the writing of celebrated authors changes in a similar way over time. With a computer algorithm, they examined the works of poet Edna St. Vincent Millay, who wrote Renascence and Other Poems (1917), along with nine other English-language writers whose careers stretched across several decades.
option a: It identifies a pattern seen in one population, introduces an inquiry concerning that pattern's presence in another population, and then details the methodology used to conduct that inquiry.
option b: It discusses an observation of a phenomenon, mentions a prediction pertaining to that phenomenon, and then evaluates two researchers' approach to testing that prediction.
option c: It provides the context for a certain inference, outlines a procedure intended to strengthen that inference, and then cites evidence produced by that procedure.
option d: It summarizes study results, notes a likely implication of those results, and then indicates how a particular technology has been used to confirm that implication.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text notes a pattern in one group, poses a question about another group, then describes the method used.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Gouache is a method that artists have used since at least the thirty-first century BCE. ______ using opaque watercolors to produce a matte finish. For an instance of the method, look at Sonia Delaunay's 1942 work Rhythm Colour.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Singular 'It' agrees with the singular subject Gouache.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? London's National Portrait Gallery (NPG) contains thousands of portraits of famous figures from British history, and among them are self-portraits by notable British artists, such as one by John Opie. ______ in most NPG portraits, the sitter is someone other than--and more famous than--the artist who painted the work.
option a: Furthermore, Opie's portrait exemplifies the museum's bias in favor of autoportraiture:
option b: Of course, such portraits are anomalies in the context of the museum's collection:
option c: However, Opie's portrait is not the only self-portrait of an artist in the museum:
option d: Consequently, such portraits reinforce the museum's curatorial philosophy:
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Of course, such portraits are anomalies' sets up the contrast with the gallery's typical portraits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In a recent study of US newspapers from 1903, researchers used a contrastive bi-encoder model to group articles by content, giving similar mathematical vectors to articles on related subjects and dissimilar vectors to those on unrelated ones. ______ they found that the largest such group was made up of articles about the Panama Canal Treaty--making it 1903's most heavily covered news story.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Ultimately' introduces the final conclusion the researchers reached.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "delicate" most nearly mean? The following passage is adapted from Kenneth Grahame's 1908 novel The Wind in the Willows. After becoming lost in the woods, the Mole has been located by a friend, and snow is starting to fall.
The Mole saw the wood that had been so dreadful to him in quite a changed aspect. Holes, hollows, pools, pitfalls, and other menaces to the wayfarer were vanishing fast, and a gleaming carpet was springing up everywhere, that looked too delicate to be trodden upon by rough feet.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The snow looked too fragile to be stepped on, so 'delicate' means fragile.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Smartwatches and similar compact electronic gadgets often hold batteries that cannot be easily ______ and replaced with new ones. Climate researcher Chloe Mikolajczak cautions that, since these batteries can't be taken out once they fail, such devices have shorter life spans and soon end up as waste.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The context ('can't be taken out') shows the batteries can't easily be removed.

question:
As used in the text, what does the phrase "steals away" most nearly mean? The following text comes from Alice Moore Dunbar-Nelson's 1895 poem "In Memoriam." The speaker describes sunlight entering a cathedral.
The light streams through the windows arched high, And o'er the stern, stone carvings breaks In warm rich gold and crimson waves, Then steals away in corners dark to die.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The light quietly departs into dark corners, so 'steals away' means slips away.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Yupno people of the isolated Finisterre Range in Papua New Guinea neither count age nor possess any artificial devices (such as clocks) for keeping track of time, yet this does not mean the Yupno are ______ time. As Rafael Núñez and colleagues recently demonstrated, the Yupno language holds numerous temporal expressions, among them kalip bishap, which translates as "past times."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The evidence of many temporal expressions shows the Yupno are not inattentive to time.
